O3_reason_to_dismiss: The export DOM parsers live in the export (out) packages, not import, and wrap the text as "<root>$content</root>" (domBuilder.kt:88, TextToXmlResourcesConvertor.kt:104), so a DOCTYPE cannot be placed before the root element; a solver can fairly say they are not XXE-reachable.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Real .stringsdict (Apple plist) files start with a public external DOCTYPE; an over-broad fix that rejects any DOCTYPE or throws on DTD (e.g. disallow-doctype-decl on the StAX path) breaks legitimate stringsdict import. Android XML/XLIFF translations also legitimately carry inline tags/CDATA that the export-side DOM parse must keep (fallback to text at domBuilder.kt:94-96).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An XLIFF 2.0 processor (version branch at XliffFileProcessor.kt:30-33 currently rejects non-1.2) with its own inline XMLInputFactory/DocumentBuilder.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The version switch is an obvious extension point; a maintainer adding 2.0 support would copy the reader setup or use a DOM parser for the richer model.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: TBX (XML glossary interchange) import next to the existing CSV glossary parser, in the ee module.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: TBX is the standard glossary format; a second implementation at distance (other Gradle module, ee package) that report-led solvers would not search.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A helper that re-parses a captured XML value block (e.g. to normalise inline tags) with a fresh default factory.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Block parsers already consume StAX events for XML-in-value content; re-parsing the block as a string is a plausible refactor and is how-type (producer the processor check never calls).
